text:
maya: Quick sync — runtime perf sprint smoke-check. Can owners confirm milestone state for: kernel microbatch PR, continuous-batch rollout, and KV eviction tweak?
omar: Kernel PR is merged to canary but not promoted. Seeing 8-12ms p95 regressions on long-token flows. Investigating. :eyes:
jenn: Continuous batch rollout is at 60% of capacity, autoscale looks stable. One customer saw higher latency at coldstart — suspect warmup ordering.
kai: KV eviction tweak PR (https://git.internal/r/redwood/pr/482) is open, pending perf test. It's the adaptive-lru change I mentioned — should reduce cache churn for short-lived keys.
maya: TY. Ownership: who will take the kernel regressions? @omar can you drive? Also need someone to own rollback plan if canary goes bad.
omar: I'll take the kernel triage. Plan: repro with the synthetic long-token test, gather profile, and open hotpatch PR if needed. If p95 > baseline for > 2hrs, we revert the canary.
jenn: I'll own the warmup ordering for continuous batching. Quick note: I added a throttling flag to avoid over-eager prefetch during scale-up. Patch in staging.
lee: I can do the rollback automation hook — will add a canary watchbook entry and a `deploy-bot` alert integration.
deploy-bot: [deploy] canary-promote pipeline started for runtime-canary-v6. Logs: http://ci.internal/logs/9876 :shipit:
kai: Quick perf test suggestion: run this locally against canary nodes: ```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -X POST https://canary.redwood/api/v1/generate -d '{"input":"x"*1024}' -o /tmp/canary_resp.json
jq '.latency_ms' /tmp/canary_resp.json | stats
```
maya: Good. Omar — if you find kernel-level hotspots, ping me and infra-replay for a flamegraph. Also, can we add a lightweight smoke test into the canary job that fails on >5% p95 regression?
omar: Yup. I'll add an e2e perf gate that runs the long-token profile and reports to CI. If it fails, the pipeline stops and notify #incidents.
jenn: One more dep note: the warmup change depends on the prefetch reorder PR from @lee (merged yesterday). If we roll back that, warmup may regress. Let's mark that as a dependency for rollbacks.
lee: Noted. I'll annotate the rollback runbook with that dependency and the exact commit hash.
maya: OK owners summary: Omar -> kernel triage + CI perf gate. Jenn -> continuous-batch warmup + throttling. Kai -> monitor KV tweak PR perf runs. Lee -> rollback automation + runbook. I'll do stakeholder update in the morning. Ping here with statuses. :thumbsup:
omar: First action: repro now, will post logs to the thread (short) when I have a profile. ETA 1.5h.
jenn: Rolling a small staging canary with the throttling flag now. ETA 20m.
kai: Running perf suite on KV PR — will share flamegraphs if anything odd.
deploy-bot: [alert] canary-watch: runtime-canary-v6 p95 spike detected (10.4ms vs baseline 3.1ms) — notified: @omar, @maya.
omar: Saw alert, pulling logs. Crashpoint looks like kernel kernel/attention.c at seq=2048. Investigating memory access patterns.
maya: If this spikes again, initiate rollback plan. Lee, can your automation trigger quick rollback and notify #eng-runtime?
lee: Yes — I have a scripted rollback that flips the traffic routing and posts to #eng-runtime + #incidents. I won't run it unless we agree or alert trips threshold.
omar: Update: found a hot loop introduced by the microbatch scheduling change. Quick fix looks small. Opening PR now and tagging @maya for review. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/pr/490
maya: Reviewing now. If green, let's ship hotfix to canary and measure. Thanks all.
jen n: (typo) jenn: Leaving a note — please add the test case for seq length 2048 to the regression suite so this doesn't slip.
maya: Good catch. Adding to sprint backlog now.
omar: Posting minimal repro logs: ```
TRACE kernel: attention_loop seq=2048 iter=34 cpu_ms=12.3
TRACE kv: cache_miss key=ctx_abc size=12
```
maya: Great thread — small actions. We'll reconvene if rollback triggers or hotfix fails. Otherwise, morning async status update from me. :coffee:
